artworks.title: Jason Taming the Bulls of Aeëtes
artworks.description: De Troy's Jason taming Aeëtes' fire-breathing bulls — the first Colchian labour Medea's charms let him survive.

artworks.title: Jason and the Dragon (Douris cup)
artworks.description: The Douris cup: Jason and the Dragon — the sleepless serpent that guards the Fleece at the trial's end.

artworks.title: Jason and Medea
artworks.description: Waterhouse's Jason and Medea — the Colchian enchantress preparing the drugs that make the king's trials survivable.

artworks.title: Meeting of Jason and King Aeëtes
artworks.description: Carracci's Meeting of Jason and King Aeëtes — the court where the impossible labours are set.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Harryhausen's Colchis — fire-breathing bulls, sown warriors, and Medea's charm — remains cinema's definitive trial for the fleece.

popCulture.title: Argonautica
popCulture.creator: Apollonius of Rhodes
popCulture.description: Books III–IV — Eros' arrow, Aeetes' tasks, and Medea's pharmaka that alone let Jason yoke the bulls and sow the teeth.

popCulture.title: Medea
popCulture.description: The Colchian priestess who chooses Jason over her father — the trials begin her exile and her power.

popCulture.title: Jason
popCulture.description: The captain who needed a sorceress more than a crew — Colchis defines him more than Iolcus ever did.
